subject: Recap: caching assumptions, budget range & effective unit economics (Cloudway POC)

Subject: Recap: caching assumptions, budget range & effective unit economics (Cloudway POC)

Alex — thanks for the call today. Quick written recap so we have a shared baseline before I update the pricing sheet. Notes below are intentionally concise; please flag anything I misremember.

Call summary
- Use case: in-product assistant for customer support agents (chat + single-turn context for KB lookups). Expected behavior: mostly short exchanges (avg ~80 tokens/request), heavy reuse of prompts and KB prefixes across sessions.
- POC goals: verify latency under 300ms median, validate prefix-cache hit behavior on representative traffic, measure quality vs quantized model.

Key asks from Redwood to finalize a pricing sketch
- Monthly token volume: please confirm low / expected / peak ranges (we discussed 80M–250M/month ranges).
- Target $/1M tokens budget: what ballpark should we aim for as a commercial target (you mentioned $350–500/1M in the call; confirm).
- Workload details: percent of repeated prompts, % multi-turn vs single-turn, and session length distribution (helps refine prefix cache hit estimate).

Caching assumptions we proposed on the call (high level)
- Prefix cache (session/prompt-level): we expect the bulk of repeated KB queries and templated prompts to hit here. For chat-heavy, templated flows we use a conservative 30–40% hit rate initially.
- KV/response cache: short deterministic responses (KB lookups, slotted templates) can add another ~5–15% depending on freshness requirements.
- Effective billed tokens = total tokens * (1 - combined_cache_hit_rate). Batching/quantization reduce compute cost but do not reduce billed token counts for external metered pricing unless cached.

Preliminary commercial example (will flesh in the spreadsheet):
- Baseline list price (model + infra) assumed for this sketch: $600 / 1M tokens
- If combined cache hit = 40% ⇒ effective billed workload = 60% ⇒ nominal effective $/1M = 0.60 * $600 = $360
- Add workload-level optimizations (batching/quantization) we model a further ~15% compute reduction ⇒ effective unit econ on infra side ≈ $306 / 1M (this is internal; final customer price may include margin/discount)

Next steps / asks
1) Confirm monthly volumes (low/expected/peak) and target $/1M.
2) Share a small sample of production request logs or synthetic profile (session lengths and repeat rates) — even anonymized summaries help.
3) We’ll send an updated pricing workbook that enumerates 3 scenarios (no-cache / conservative-cache / optimistic-cache) and shows the resulting effective $/1M under each.

I attached a draft pricing workbook and a quick CSV template to capture cache patterns. I’ll follow-up internally with a firm POC proposal and suggested kickoff date.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Recap: caching assumptions, budget range & effective unit economics (Cloudway POC)

Alex — great, thanks for the ranges and the detail on repeats. Quick answers, plus a worked example so we’re aligned on how we compute the effective unit economics.

Billing and caching (concise)
- If Redwood serves a full response from a prefix cache (i.e., we do not execute model decoder steps), the customer is not billed CPU tokens for that response. Billed tokens = number of model tokens processed (input + output) for non-cached model executions.
- Prefix cache applies at prompt-level matching: for multi-turn sessions, if the current prompt (including session context we consider for matching) matches a cached key we will serve from cache. In practice, that means highly templated multi-turn flows see good cross-turn benefit when prompts reuse the same prefixes.

Worked example (conservative assumptions you can tweak)
- Baseline list price (model + infra): $600 / 1M tokens (placeholder for workbook)
- Traffic: 110M tokens/month (expected)
- Cache assumptions: prefix hit 35% (templated prompts), KV/response cache 5% ⇒ combined cache hit = 40%
- Effective billed tokens = 110M * (1 - 0.40) = 66M billed tokens
- Effective billed unit price = 0.60 * $600 = $360 / 1M billed tokens ⇒ monthly cost = 66 * $360 ≈ $23,760
- With additional compute optimizations (batching + quantization) we model a 15% reduction in infra compute cost; applying that to the $360 gives ≈ $306 / 1M effective
- If you want committed capacity (12mo) we can layer a 20% committed discount in the workbook ⇒ ~$245 / 1M effective in that scenario

I’ve updated the attached workbook with these three scenarios (no-cache / conservative-cache / committed-discount). I added a column for sensitivity analysis so we can quickly see effect at 30/40/50% hit rates.

Next steps (short)
- Please send the anonymized sample/summary (dev export) — Neha listed below can coordinate the secure upload.
- If the $245–360 / 1M effective band roughly maps to your internal target, we’ll prepare a formal POC SOW and a 12mo committed-capacity pricing term.

I’ll also propose a short (30m) technical sync to walk the team through caching semantics and the request-to-keying logic. Rafael can drive that with your infra folks.

Thanks,
Ben
